claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024 reports: After 2021 and 2023 were Kosovo's hottest years, family medicine centres in Pristina and Mitrovica reported more child admissions, especially above 30°C.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Facility-reported association with hot conditions; no counts, population denominator or isolated temperature effect.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024 reports: Early-2023 floods affected about 22,000 people, including 3,000 children, mostly in Skenderaj and Mitrovica. Average-year floods affect about 10,000 people, damaging homes/schools and interrupting water and power.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF flags disabled/health-condition and Roma, Ashkali and Egyptian children as facing added challenges; fires increased since 2007 in Mitrovica and Prizren, while human-caused fires removed 13% of Kosovo tree cover in 2001–2023.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Group-specific vulnerability and geographically distinct fire findings are separate findings; not all fires or associated tree-cover loss are climate-caused.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2023 reports: KMAC weighs risk, environment/development and poverty in site priorities; hazards contributing to climate impacts receive top clearance priority. Operators lacked climate-specific procedures at report time.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2023 reports: War ordnance contaminated wooded hills west of Peja, which faces flash floods, hotter summers and milder, less snowy winters. Clearance released 355,502 m², reopening park trails and resource access.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Reported land release and restored resource access, not measured avoided climate losses or a causal peace outcome.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2023 reports: In Mitrovica, war/industrial-closure migration and weakened services coexist with hotter summers, less snow and possible July–August drought. Clearance restored Barë grazing/firewood access and Bajgora woodland/pipeline access; wind power was exported.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Qualitative historical access/restoration case; summer drought is potential, and climate-resilience benefits are described as incidental, not independently quantified.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2022-11 reports: The plan flags women in rural Prizren as potentially responsible for agricultural water management yet having limited water access; it calls for women's participation in planning, early warnings and drought-tolerant seed support.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-08-05 reports: A June–July 2026 Podujeva survey of 101 respondents across 35 settlements found recurrent, materially damaging floods among participating households, with impacts concentrated on agricultural land and crops.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: The non-representative Podujeva survey summary reports drinking-water interruptions, drainage/maintenance gaps and uneven warning access among respondents.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Item-specific denominators vary; precise warning percentages are omitted because the full report was inaccessible.

executive_assessment.text: Local child-risk examples include Ferizaj/Prizren and Skenderaj/Mitrovica floods, while the Podujeva survey is indicative of respondents only.
Conflict-legacy ordnance constrained access to land/resources near Peja and Barë/Bajgora; clearance restored access, without quantifying climate-resilience gains.
Prizren water/land and gender priorities remain commitments whose implementation has not been verified.
